adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Hands remain free to play instruments or hold rattles.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular formation divided into four sections corresponding to cardinal directions.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Movement is restricted to the torso.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Outer circle dancers perform more vibrant movements including leaps.
movement_profile.partnering: Dancers do not touch each other.
movement_profile.posture: Upright and focused inward toward the center of the circle.

signature_moves.description: Lieutenants mark the four cardinal directions within the circle.
signature_moves.name: Cardinal marking

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Starts slow, increases in speed, then slows down near the end.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not touch other dancers; do not solicit donations (chimaleros).

music_profile.sound_description: A percussive, earthy sound dominated by the deep resonance of huehuetl and teponaztli drums, layered with the sharp, rhythmic rattling of ayoyotes and the melodic, stringed quality of the concha lute.
music_profile.vocal_style: Chanting and singing of prayers or praises.

basic_steps: Form a circle with other dancers.
Move feet and torso in rhythm with the drums.
Use hands to play instruments or shake rattles.
Follow the captain's lead for changes in speed.
teaching.formation: Circular formation with leaders in the center and dancers in concentric circles.
teaching.level_notes: Beginners typically start in the outer circle, while elders and leaders occupy the inner circle.
teaching.rhythm: The rhythm increases in speed as the dance progresses.
